s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent lesion of the nasal vestibule with local invasion
salient_findings: Recurrent lesion of the right nasal vestibule mucosa
Tumor within the nasal vestibule floor and ala
key_facts: Female patient in her 50s
Never-smoker
Initial lesion biopsied 5 years prior
Initial biopsy reported as solid and cystic hidradenoma
p63 positive, pancytokeratin positive, and p16 negative on initial biopsy
Lesion recurred 8 months prior to presentation
Second excision showed p63 positive and p16 negative with positive margins
Enlarged, firm right ala on examination
Tumor visualized within the nasal vestibule floor and ala
Imaging showed thicker right ala compared to the left ala

raw.rationale: The patient's initial biopsy was reported as a solid and cystic hidradenoma, which is a rare benign tumor, but the recurrence and aggressive behavior of the lesion, along with the positive margins on the second excision, suggest a malignant transformation to hidradenocarcinoma.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: The initial biopsy was p16 negative, which is less common in squamous cell carcinoma, and the histological description does not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Adnexal carcinoma
rejected.why: While adnexal carcinoma is a broad term that encompasses hidradenocarcinoma, the specific diagnosis of hidradenocarcinoma is more precise based on the patient's history and biopsy results.

rejected.label: Basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: The biopsy results do not support this diagnosis, as basal cell carcinoma typically has different histological and immunohistochemical characteristics.

rejected.label: Sweat gland carcinoma
rejected.why: This is a broader term that includes hidradenocarcinoma, but hidradenocarcinoma is a more specific diagnosis based on the patient's history and biopsy results.

gold: Nonkeratinizing squamous cell carcinoma of the nasal mucosa with Schneiderian features
